changes: The controller records the adapter-measured display at start_test and refuses an out-of-display tap before calling the adapter. No input is sent, the guest is not stopped, and no source write or rebuild is required. The refusal still uses one work action; cancellation and deadline expiry still stop the job.

Observations return uiSummary, and taps return afterUiSummary: bounded visible text and controls with bounds and actual-pixel centers, parsed from the guest view tree with declarations refused and size, depth, node and element limits. The view tree is timed separately from its screenshot.
The report links the post-tap view tree and counts it when unavailable.
Tool schema and skill guidance describe actual-pixel coordinates; validation errors name the rejected field and the action's accepted fields.

changes: New jobs default to 60 minutes instead of 30; the initial selection range stays 5 to 60 minutes and repeated prepare still cannot change it.

A new extend action adds 5 to 30 controller minutes with a required reason, only after a new successful build since the previous grant. A job allows at most 3 grants and 120 minutes in total including the initial selection; a request beyond that total is reduced to the remainder. The running guest's deadline moves first. Extensions add no writes, builds or actions, cannot revive an expired, cancelled or ended job, and are recorded in state and the report.
Progress receipts report granted extension minutes and remaining extensions, and state that the chat timeout is separate.

changes: android_project declares catalogMode direct-only, so OpenClaw keeps it out of the Tool Search catalog and returns its screenshots as native image blocks. Through the tool_call bridge each capture was serialized as roughly 20,000 characters of base64 text that the model could not view.
The skill now calls android_project directly and keeps tool_call only as a fallback when the tool is absent from the direct tool list.

Per-job budgets are named constants and rise from 8 writes, 3 builds and 40 actions to 20 writes, 10 builds and 120 actions. Repair eligibility after a guest failure still requires a spare write, build and three actions.

Pre-deploy review fixes: receipts stop offering extensions once the 120-minute total (which includes the initial limit) is used; a granted extension says it used one work action; the per-guest artifact cap rises from 256 to 640 files (128 MiB) so a full action budget cannot end a healthy guest; system dialogs owned by package 'android' are labelled as such in uiSummary; the tap validation error says actual display pixels instead of quoting the 0-8192 transport bound.

versions.deploymentNote: Installed with the guarded updater from exact stage4AQ files; seven files replaced with backups. No plugin change, so no Gateway refresh was needed.

changes: Jobs default to 120 controller minutes (5-240 selectable); extensions of 5-30 minutes are granted after any new successful work action (source write, build, launch, tap or observation), up to 8 grants and 240 minutes in total. Receipts warn when less than 15 minutes remain and an extension is currently grantable.

A chat session may start a continuation job after its job ends with confirmed cleanup. The session's jobs share 20 writes, 10 builds, 120 actions and 240 minutes (elapsed time, capped at each job's allotment), so ending a job never resets limits. Uncertain cleanup, exhausted limits or a cancelled session refuse continuation.

Only the plugin's cleanup after an interrupted call (request IDs ending ':abort') cancels a session; the model's own stop does not. An interruption stops every active job of the session. Work aimed at an ended job after the controller idles out is answered from the record instead of failing, so it no longer turns into a cancellation.

Replayed preparation requests never create another job; the continuation decision reads job status under the job's lock; build-failure summaries stay under the plugin's 16000-character receipt bound; refusals name the job's actual state.

Each screenshot is also saved once into OpenClaw's inbound media store and its image block gains a media://inbound url and caption, so the Control UI can show it; the model still receives the image data. Copies are deduplicated, re-saved if pruned, and capped per job.
The skill tells the model to exercise real-time games inside one tap burst, to request extensions early, how continuation works, and that prepare takes no jobId.
